title: THEY DIDN’T ATTACK.
paragraphs: THEY DIDN’T ATTACK.
They walked.

Around a city built for war.
Walls thick enough to race chariots on.
Gates sealed. Soldiers waiting.
And God said:
Walk.

Not charge.
Not climb.
Not break the gate.
Just walk.
Day one — silence.

Dust rising under thousands of feet.
Priests carrying the Ark.
Trumpets breathing slow notes into the desert wind.

No arrows.
No swords swinging.
Just… footsteps.
The people inside Jericho must have laughed.
“Is that their strategy?”

Day two.
The same strange parade.

Day three.
Still walking.

No siege engines.
No battering rams.
Just obedience.
Because sometimes the most dangerous thing you can do in a battle…
is trust God’s instructions when they make no sense.
By day six the soldiers of Israel probably felt the tension burning in their chests.

Warriors trained to fight.
But God told them to wait.
Then came day seven.
Seven laps around the city.
The silence stretched like a drawn bow.
Then Joshua gave the command.
“Shout! For the LORD has given you the city!” (Joshua 6:16)

The trumpets exploded.
The people roared.
And the walls…
collapsed.
Not cracked.
Collapsed.
Because Jericho wasn’t defeated by Israel’s strength.
It fell to God’s power and Israel’s obedience.
Listen carefully.
Most of us want God to bless our plans.
But Jericho teaches a harder truth:
Victory belongs to those who follow God’s plan, even when it looks foolish.
Sometimes faith feels like walking in circles.

Praying again.
Waiting again.
Trusting again.
And the walls don’t move.
Until suddenly…
God moves.
But there’s a deeper layer to this story.

Jericho was under judgment.
Yet one household was saved.
Rahab.

A woman with a stained past who believed the God of Israel was real.
Because grace always finds the one who turns toward God.
Even in the middle of collapsing walls.
That is the Gospel pattern.

Judgment is real.
Sin builds walls around the human heart.
But salvation still hangs from the window — like Rahab’s scarlet cord.
A picture pointing forward.
To the blood of Jesus Christ.
Because when Christ died and rose again, the greatest wall ever built — the wall between sinful humanity and a holy God — came crashing down.
Not by our strength.
By His sacrifice.
So if you feel like you're walking in circles today…
Don’t quit on the sixth lap.
The shout may be closer than you think.
And if your past feels like Rahab’s story…
Grace is still knocking.
Turn to Jesus.

Because He is the God who brings down walls —
and rebuilds lives.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
